payload.acceptance_criteria: kit-boundary refuses a kit module that imports a process-spawning or network module, names the module and the line, and passes the kit as it stands today; a test proves the refusal fires on a planted import rather than only that the tree is clean
payload.description:
When a kit module reaches the network or spawns a process, I want the boundary gate to refuse it, so I can stop section 4 asserting a property no check reads.

SPEC.md section 4 states the kit is standard library only, no third party, no network, no subprocess. kit-boundary.py checks two rules and neither is that one: does a module import basicly, and does it name an engine path. So half the declared boundary is enforced by prose.

That is the same fail-open shape section 4 itself narrates about the import linter, which analysed one root package while the kit is flat modules outside it and would have reported success forever. A boundary claim nothing reads is indistinguishable from one that passes.

Measured 2026-09-18: no kit module imports subprocess, socket, urllib, http or requests today, against a positive control that six of them import json. So the gate lands green and locks in a property that currently holds, rather than reporting a debt.
payload.requirements: the gate reads the kit's source, never runs it. No new dependency. The refusal message names what to do instead, as the two existing rules do.
payload.title: gate the half of the kit boundary that nothing enforces

payload.acceptance_criteria: basicly-tracker fsck DIR reports the fold and its findings and exits 0 clean, 1 on a stale derivative and 2 on a broken log; --rebuild writes every derivative again from the log first and names what it wrote
payload.description: When a consumer wants to know whether the log is still the truth, I want fsck behind the same entry point as every other verb, so I can check it without knowing which file inside the vendored kit to run.
payload.requirements: no new logic: the subcommand calls the checker that already exists rather than a second implementation. The standalone entry point stays under the module size cap without a waiver.
payload.title: put fsck behind the one command a consumer already knows
